name: Watermelon
summary: Watermelon is a large, juicy fruit with sweet red flesh, eaten fresh or as juice. This page lists what people say watermelon does; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: Watermelon holds L-citrulline, an amino acid found in high concentrations in it, which may help the body make more nitric oxide. It also holds polyphenols and lycopene, according to a 2026 meta-analysis.

The UK food table (CoFID) measures watermelon flesh at 31 kcal, 7.1 g of sugars, 100 mg of potassium, 8 mg of vitamin C and 19 µg of vitamin A (as retinol equivalents) per 100 g. It has no fibre value for it, and it does not measure citrulline or lycopene.

tableFoods.label: 1 slice of watermelon, flesh only (about 200 g)

processing: The rind is not the flesh: a 2026 lab study separated L-citrulline from watermelon rind juice, so the rind holds some too.
Weight with or without rind changes the table's numbers: 18 kcal per 100 g weighed whole, against 31 kcal for flesh only.

whoShouldBeCareful.note: A published case report describes high blood potassium in a person with end-stage kidney disease after eating a great deal of watermelon, and a 2018 review says a dietary potassium limit is usually recommended in reduced kidney function. The UK food table lists 100 mg of potassium per 100 g of flesh, so the amount eaten matters. If you have kidney disease, talk to your doctor or dietitian.

Watermelon can cause allergic reactions. A study of 23 allergic patients found three major allergens in it: malate dehydrogenase, triose phosphate isomerase and profilin. If you react to watermelon, talk to your doctor or an allergist.

unknowns: Whether the blood pressure results of trials carry over to eating watermelon at ordinary amounts: the 2026 meta-analysis pooled trials of watermelon, its juice and its extract.
How much citrulline and lycopene a given watermelon holds: the food table does not measure them.
Which fruit the Roman word 'pepo' meant: the translator of Pliny's Natural History reads it as a pumpkin or gourd, so this page has no Then and now entries for watermelon.
